title: Steps declare the authority they write: the run derives from intent x seat

rollback: The series reverts cleanly: `seat` is an additive field on SetupState and on the GET /api/me/onboarding body, the predicates treat a null seat as today's full run, and no server write, table or route method changes - reverting restores the intent-only predicates with nothing persisted to migrate.
runner_up: One server finish door (POST /api/me/onboarding/finish): the wizard posts its answers once, the server resolves authority once, runs every write and the stamp in one request, and answers the folded outcome - replacing 3 server actions + 5 route doors fired from the client.
body:
## Summary
Give every setup step a declared write requirement (the capability its answers need) and make the caller's seat part of the wizard's state, so `relevantSteps()`, the rail, the counter, `finishPartsFor()` and the hand-off's exits all derive from intent x seat. An invited recruiter stops being walked through an owner's setup whose every answer the server refuses.

## Description
The '/' gate is per user (onboarding-gate.ts:26-29) and a redeemed invite lands on '/' (invite-result.ts:100-101), so the wizard's most frequent audience after the owner is the owner's teammates. The step model knows only the intent (setupSteps.ts:55-64). A recruiter or admin is asked to type the company name (required, blank on their browser - SetupCompanyStep.tsx:64-71), pick a currency and brand, stage invites, and finishes into ORG_SETTINGS_FORBIDDEN on name, currency and language (org-actions.ts:54-103; language is written on every run, setupOnboardingFinish.ts:34,58) and a 403 on every invite (org/invites/route.ts:32). Two answers do land and should not: the brand PUT is operator-gated only (brand/route.ts:51-53), so an invitee's accent pick re-skins the app for the whole org, and the Recommended tour tile starts a pipeline-writing run for a viewer (SetupHandoffSummary.tsx:137-139 vs navCapabilities.ts:39-41).

The move: steps declare `requires?: Capability` beside `relevant` (company -> org:manage, team -> members:manage, pipeline -> pipeline:write); `SetupState.seat: Capability[] | null` is read once from GET /api/me/onboarding (which already serves `scope` and is ungated for the same reason /api/me/capabilities is), computed as callerOrgCapabilities() union callerCapabilities() - exactly the two resolvers the finish doors gate on. `relevantSteps` filters on both predicates; `finishPartsFor` already derives from walked steps and additionally drops the org-wide language write without org:manage; `handoffExits(seat)` drops the tour without pipeline:write. A null seat is today's run (fail-open, like navCapabilities), so the server stays the enforcement and the keyless e2e journey (open mode = owner fold) is unchanged.

## Flow
1. `setupSeat.ts` (pure): SetupSeat type, parseSetupSeat(body), seatAllows(seat, cap) with null = allow, handoffExits(seat).
2. setupSteps.ts: `requires` on the three steps; relevantSteps checks `relevant` AND seatAllows; INITIAL_SETUP.seat = null.
3. GET /api/me/onboarding adds `seat: { capabilities }`; useSetupDraft.ts already fetches this route for `scope` - it hands the seat to the host via update({ seat }) from the same response (one fetch, not two).
4. setupOnboardingFinish.ts: finishPartsFor pushes 'language' only when seatAllows(seat, 'org:manage').
5. SetupHandoffSummary.tsx renders the exits handoffExits returns; a join-run title key (no Company step walked) in 4 catalogs.
6. Tests first (the 8 cases), then the implementation; app-structure.md's shell/setup section gains the seat axis.

## Expected impact
Every invited teammate's first five minutes: 6 steps with a required field they cannot answer and a red 3-to-5-part refusal toast become a 3-to-5-step run whose every answer lands. Two live mis-writes close (an invitee's accent re-skinning the org; a viewer starting a data-writing tour). Owner and open-mode runs are unchanged by construction.

## Evaluation
Claim: the wizard's step sequence, finish parts and hand-off exits are derived from intent x seat, and an unknown seat reproduces today's run.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no seat field, no requires, no handoffExits, GET /api/me/onboarding answers scope only).
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - node:test over setupSeat.test.ts, setupSteps.test.ts, setupOnboardingFinish.test.ts and app/api/me/onboarding/route.test.ts, plus the existing journey-role-to-schedule e2e unchanged (open mode folds to owner).
Result: pending build.
Gate: npm run test:unit, tsc, lint, i18n:check.

title: Finish ends on a receipt: share each invite link, retry only what failed
acceptance: sendSetupInvites with a 200 body { invite: { token: 'inv-abc' } } -> the landed result carries token 'inv-abc'; with the existing test stub body { invite: {} } -> ok true, token null (setupOnboardingFinish.test.ts:29-38 keeps passing)

finishReceipt(results, 'https://kp.example') with two landed invites -> links [{ email, url: 'https://kp.example/invite/inv-abc' }, ...] in staged order, built by the same publicBaseUrl rule copyInviteUrl uses; a landed invite with a null token yields no link and is counted in `unshareable`
finishReceipt with no landed invites and an ok outcome -> null, so finish() closes exactly as today (the journey-role-to-schedule e2e, which stages no invites, is unchanged)

isRetryable(failure): code null, 'TOO_MANY_REQUESTS' or any '*_FAILED' store code -> true; 'ORG_SETTINGS_FORBIDDEN', 'INVITE_ALREADY_MEMBER', 'INVITE_ROLE_ABOVE_PRIVILEGE', 'BRAND_ACCENT_ILLEGIBLE_LIGHT' -> false (a permanent refusal is named, never offered a Retry that cannot work)

finishRemainder(state, results) after orgName landed, invites jana landed + petr refused (code null), pipeline refused 409 -> a state whose finishPartsFor-run touches ONLY invites [petr] and pipeline; retrying it posts one invite (petr) and never re-mints jana's token or re-calls setOrgName

finishNext(outcome, receipt): receipt null -> 'close'; receipt non-null -> 'receipt'; the '/api/me/onboarding' completed stamp and clearDraft run on the receipt's Done, not in finish()'s finally, and the tour tile's sim.start() waits for that Done

(messages/en.json:7338) and copies via copyInviteUrl (app/features/settings/workspace/workspaceAdminHelpers.ts:14-16, WorkspaceTab.tsx:244-245)

app/features/shell/setup/OnboardingExperience.tsx:240-248 - clearDraft(), stamp('completed') and onClose() run in `finally` whatever the outcome, so a partial finish drops every answer, closes the wizard and (via useSetupUnfinished, which reads the completed stamp) removes the board's resume door - the only record of what failed is the transient toast at :236
app/features/shell/setup/setupFinishOutcome.ts:46-48 already carries a per-part refused code and the refused invite addresses - the data a targeted retry needs exists and is thrown away
app/features/shell/setup/SetupHandoffSummary.tsx:137-139 - the tour tile fires ctrl.finish() and sim.start() in the same tick, so the tour starts while the finish writes are still in flight

Registry wizard-flows/commit-boundary: 'Make the retry safe. Re-confirming after a partial failure re-runs only the failed and unattempted parts' and 'Terminal ... the surface shows what was created and where to live with it now'
rollback: Reverts cleanly: the token field is additive on SetupInviteResult, the receipt is a new pane rendered in place of the step grid (the same slot SetupLeaveConfirm uses), and restoring the old finally block restores today's close-on-finish; no server route, table or stored shape changes.
runner_up: Make the leave confirmation's 'Nothing is lost' true: dismiss() keeps the draft (OnboardingExperience.tsx:171 clears it) so the board's resume door reopens the wizard with the answers instead of a blank form (likely S alone).
body:
## Summary
When finish() has something the operator must act on, the wizard stays open on a receipt instead of closing under a toast: one copyable accept link per invite it minted (plus Copy all), and each part that did not land, with Retry offered only where a retry can work and running only the failed parts. With nothing to act on it closes exactly as today.

## Description
kp sends no invite mail - the route mints a tokenized link for the UI to share (org/invites/route.ts:29-30, invites.ts:50-72). The Organization console knows this ('Copy the link to share it', en.json:7338). The wizard does not: it discards the token on success (setupOnboardingFinish.ts:158), tells the operator '2 teammates invited' (en.json:9556) and closes. The invitees never hear of it; the operator learns only by finding Settings -> Organization -> pending invites. Separately, a partial finish is unrecoverable: clearDraft, the completed stamp and onClose run in `finally` regardless of the fold (OnboardingExperience.tsx:240-248), so a network blip on the axis write or one refused invite throws away the answers and the resume door, leaving a toast as the only record - while the fold already knows exactly which parts and addresses failed (setupFinishOutcome.ts:46-48).

The leap: finish() computes a receipt (pure, setupFinishOutcome.ts): links for landed invites, failures split into retryable (null code, rate limit, store *_FAILED) and permanent (forbidden, already-member, illegible accent). If the receipt is empty the flow is today's. Otherwise SetupFinishReceipt replaces the step grid (the SetupLeaveConfirm slot, same fixed card height): the links with copy buttons, the permanent refusals named via useErrorMessage, and Retry that re-runs finishRemainder(state, results) - only the failed parts, only the refused addresses, never re-minting a landed token. The stamp and the draft clear move to the receipt's Done, and the tour tile's sim.start() waits for it.

## Flow
1. setupFinishOutcome.ts: SetupInviteResult.token; finishReceipt(results, origin); isRetryable(failure); finishRemainder(state, results); finishNext(outcome, receipt).
2. setupOnboardingFinish.ts: sendSetupInvites reads body.invite.token; persistOnboardingSetup returns the raw part results beside the fold.
3. OnboardingExperience.tsx: finish -> receipt state; retryFinish(); closeReceipt() stamps 'completed', clears the draft, runs any deferred sim.start, closes.
4. setupSteps.ts OnboardingCtrl gains receipt / retryFinish / closeReceipt; SetupOnboardingWizard.tsx renders the receipt pane in place of the grid.
5. SetupHandoffSummary.tsx: honest meta copy ('links to share'); tour tile defers the start.
6. 4 catalogs; app-structure.md shell/setup section.

## Expected impact
Every invite staged in the wizard becomes a link the operator actually has in hand at the moment they are thinking about their team, instead of a pending row nobody is told about. A partial finish stops costing the operator their answers: the failed parts are retried in place, the refused ones are named with their reason, and the first-run resume door is not closed on an unfinished setup.

## Evaluation
Claim: finish surfaces every minted invite as a shareable link and re-runs only failed, retryable parts; with nothing to act on it closes as today.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (token discarded, no receipt, no remainder, stamp in finally).
After: 7 of 7.
Method: gate - node:test over setupFinishOutcome.test.ts and setupOnboardingFinish.test.ts (fetch stubbed as the file already does), i18n:check for the copy case; journey-role-to-schedule e2e unchanged (it stages no invites, so receipt is null).
Result: pending build.
Gate: npm run test:unit, tsc, lint, i18n:check.
